procedure.description: percutaneous transcatheter placement of intracoronary stent, single major coronary artery

denial.carcText: The procedure code is inconsistent with the modifier used.
denial.text: Prairie Commons Medicaid Plan denied the claim for CPT 92928 (percutaneous transcatheter placement of intracoronary stent, single major coronary artery) with date of service 2026-02-03. CARC 4: The procedure code is inconsistent with the modifier used. Payer remark: Modifier 59 was billed on the stent line together with modifier LD; the combination is invalid for this code. Resubmit a corrected claim.

criteria.text: Angina of Canadian Cardiovascular Society class II to IV persisting despite at least two antianginal medications at optimal doses, or documented intolerance.

Objective evidence of ischemia: stress imaging showing a moderate or large reversible defect (10 percent or more of the myocardium), or invasive physiology with fractional flow reserve of 0.80 or less or instantaneous wave-free ratio of 0.89 or less in the target vessel.
Angiographic stenosis of 70 percent or more in the target vessel (50 to 69 percent with abnormal invasive physiology).

chart.text: Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for evaluation. His history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end.
Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.
A1c came back 6.1. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. He is motivated.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 2.9, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 75. Repeat in a year.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
He called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in early summer. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.

60 year old man in cardiology clinic with exertional chest pressure for 8 months, relieved by rest. Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, family history of early coronary disease. Stress imaging ordered, medications reviewed and continued. His history otherwise: migraines, rare now. Allergies: codeine makes him sick. Quit smoking 3 years ago, no alcohol, stays home with the kids. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Mole on the right calf that his spouse noticed. About 6 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change he is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Vitamin D came back 16. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Patient called about a tick bite on the calf after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.

Regadenoson SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging. Large reversible perfusion defect of the anterior wall and apex, 13 percent of the left ventricle, with transient ischemic dilation. Ejection fraction 54 percent post-stress.
Metoprolol succinate 100 daily, amlodipine 10 daily, isosorbide mononitrate 60 daily, all at these doses for the past 5 months. Aspirin 81, atorvastatin 80.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. He mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Reviewed the stress test. Given the size of the defect and ongoing symptoms on maximal medical therapy, recommended coronary angiography with physiology and intervention if appropriate. Risks reviewed, he agrees. Vitals today 119 over 68, pulse 68. Still class III angina walking one block or climbing a flight despite three antianginal medications at target doses, using nitroglycerin 6 times a week.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, he will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Here with a cough and congestion for 9 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 18 and 14. No ocular pathology noted.

Coronary angiography. Proximal left anterior descending 89 percent stenosis. Fractional flow reserve across the lesion 0.72. Circumflex and right coronary without significant disease. Proceeded to intervention of the proximal left anterior descending: predilation and a 3.5 by 18 millimeter drug-eluting stent, TIMI 3 flow, no residual stenosis.

expected.note: CARC 4 is an administrative denial the chart cannot answer: the remedy is a corrected claim with the right modifier, not a medical necessity appeal.
